Provision: RESTRICTIVE GOVERNANCE PROVISION 1. [Government] [must] [create or appoint agency to implement and enforce the law] [at law’s commencement] [or else it is negligent in its duties]
Evidence: Article 19(2): "The body that has rendered a decision on state registration of a charitable organization shall exert control over the compliance of activity of the charitable organization with the goals for the sake of which it has been established."
Explanation: The statute itself designates (i.e., appoints) the authority that registers charitable organizations as the body responsible for ongoing control and enforcement of the law. By identifying that body and assigning it enforcement duties in the text that takes effect upon the law’s commencement, the law fulfills the requirement of appointing an agency to implement and enforce the law. Therefore the correct label is 1.

Provision: PERMISSIVE GOVERNANCE PROVISION 1. [Agency] [must] [explain penalty for particular offenses, or explain a ‘general penalty’ for offenses where no penalty is expressly provided] [before commencement of the law] [or else it is negligent in its duties]
Evidence: Article 20(1): "In the cases of its violating the present Federal Law, the charitable organization shall be held responsible in conformity with the legislation of the Russian Federation."
Explanation: The statute itself sets out a catch-all liability clause stating that any breach of the law will trigger responsibility under the broader Russian legal framework. This functions as a general penalty provision covering offenses for which no specific sanction is detailed. Although the duty is not phrased as an obligation on a particular agency, the law text fulfils the matrix requirement by providing a general penalty mechanism prior to its commencement. Therefore the presence label (1) is correct.

Provision: RESTRICTIVE GOVERNANCE PROVISION 2. [CSOs] [must] [accept restricted freedoms on certain matters] [after law’s commencement] [or else face penalty for non-compliance]
Evidence: Art. 12(3): "A charitable organization shall have the right to engage in business activities only to achieve the goals, for the sake of which it was set up..."; Art. 20(4): "All the means earned by the charity organization in performing business activities in violation of Article 12 of the present Federal Law shall be exacted into the revenue of the local budget..."
Explanation: The statute explicitly limits a charitable organization’s freedom to conduct business: it may do so ONLY when the activities advance its statutory goals (Art. 12(3)).  Any violation triggers a concrete sanction—confiscation of related proceeds (Art. 20(4)).  Thus the law requires CSOs to accept a specific restriction after the law’s commencement and provides a penalty for non-compliance, satisfying the matrix provision. Therefore the original label of presence (1) is correct.

Provision: PERMISSIVE GOVERNANCE PROVISION 2. [Government and agency] [must] [create or empower a dispute resolution forum] such as a court [before commencement of the law]
Evidence:
Article 9(3): "The decision on the refusal of the state registration of a charitable organization ... may be appealed against with the court."  
Article 20(2): "... the charitable organization may appeal against [a written warning] in the court."
Explanation: By expressly allowing appeals of registration refusals and administrative warnings to a court, the statute itself grants jurisdiction to the judiciary over disputes between CSOs and the registering body. This constitutes an explicit empowerment of a dispute-resolution forum (the court) within the law. Hence the provision is present, so the first-round coder’s label of 1 is correct.

Provision: RESTRICTIVE GOVERNANCE PROVISION 3. [Government] [may] [create or empower cabinet minister to make new rules regulating CSOs on certain matters] [after law’s commencement] [or else leave the regulatory regime unchanged]
Evidence: Art. 3(1) states that legislation on charitable activities consists of the Constitution, Civil Code, this Federal Law, and other federal laws and regional laws; it does not mention any authority for the Government or a cabinet minister to issue additional regulations. The only later reference (Art. 25) merely orders the Government to align its existing acts with this law, not to make new rules regulating CSOs.
Explanation: To satisfy this matrix provision, the statute must expressly authorize the Government—or empower a cabinet minister—to promulgate subordinate regulations concerning CSOs after the law comes into force. The cited Article 3(1) simply lists the hierarchy of laws and does not provide such rule-making authority. Article 25 instructs the Government to bring its own acts into conformity with the law, but that is an implementation directive, not an empowerment to create new regulations governing CSOs. Because no clause grants the Government discretionary power to issue future CSO rules, the provision is absent, so the correct label is 0.

Provision: PERMISSIVE GOVERNANCE PROVISION 3. [CSOs] [may] [adopt standards for self-regulation through associations] [after law’s commencement] [or else choose not to be self-regulated]
Evidence: Article 14(1) merely states: “The charitable organizations shall have the right to unite into associations and unions, created on the contractual basis to expand their opportunities in realizing the goals set out in their Rules.” The remainder of Article 14 contains no language on establishing or adopting self-regulatory standards.
Explanation: The matrix provision requires that the law explicitly allow CSOs to adopt self-regulatory standards through their associations. Article 14 grants a right to form associations and unions, but it does not mention developing or adopting standards for self-regulation. Because the specific Aim component (“adopt standards for self-regulation”) is missing, the provision is not implemented in the statute. Hence the correct label is 0 (absence).

Provision: RESTRICTIVE GOVERNANCE PROVISION 4. [Agency] [may] [publish certain information about a CSO, or seize CSO property and documents] [with or without reasonable cause after law’s commencement] [or else choose other tactics to receive information from CSOs]
Evidence: Article 19(4): "The body that has rendered a decision on the state registration of a charitable organization SHALL provide for an open access ... to the given charitable organizations' annual reports it has received."
Explanation: The matrix provision contemplates a permissive power ("may") for the agency to publish information or seize property/documents. Article 19(4) instead imposes a mandatory duty ("shall provide") on the registration body to disclose annual reports. Because the deontic element is obligatory rather than permissive, the law does not confer discretionary authority as required by the matrix provision. No other section grants such discretionary powers. Therefore, the provision is absent (0).

Provision: RESTRICTIVE GOVERNANCE PROVISION 6. [Non-state actors] [must not] [create new CSOs] because only the state may do so [or else face penalty for non-compliance]
Evidence: Article 8: "The founders of a charitable organization, depending on its form, shall be the natural and (or) the legal persons. The state power bodies and the local self-government bodies … shall not be the founders of a charitable organization."
Explanation: The matrix provision would bar non-state actors from establishing CSOs. Article 8 of the law expressly grants founding rights to private natural and legal persons and even forbids state bodies from being founders. This is the direct opposite of the matrix rule, so the provision is explicitly negated. Therefore the correct label is ‑1, matching the first-round coder.

Provision: PERMISSIVE FORMATION PROVISION 1. [Agency] [must] [follow explicit termination and dissolution provisions] [when attempting to cancel or suspended a CSO] [or else it is negligent in its duties]
Evidence: Art. 20(2)-(3): when the registering body issues repeated written warnings, "the charitable organization may be liquidated in conformity with the procedure, stipulated by the Civil Code of the Russian Federation."  Art. 11(1): "The reorganization and the liquidation of a charitable organization shall be effected in conformity with the law-stipulated procedure."
Explanation: The statute imposes a mandatory duty that liquidation (cancellation) of a charitable organization be carried out strictly according to the specific procedures set out in other governing laws (the Civil Code).  The obligation is triggered when the registering body (i.e., the competent agency) seeks to liquidate the CSO after warnings, and the text uses deontic language ("shall be effected in conformity with…").  This satisfies the matrix requirement that the agency must follow explicit termination-and-dissolution provisions when cancelling or suspending a CSO.  Therefore the presence label (1) assigned by the first-round coder is correct.

Provision: RESTRICTIVE FORMATION PROVISION 2. [CSOs] [must not] [appeal the registration denial or deregistration order] [after such a decision has been communicated] [or else face penalty for non-compliance]
Evidence: Article 9(3): "The decision on the refusal of the state registration of a charitable organization, and also its avoidance of such registration, may be appealed against with the court."
Explanation: The matrix provision would prohibit CSOs from appealing a denial of registration. Article 9(3) does the opposite: it explicitly grants CSOs the right to appeal such decisions in court. Because the law affirmatively permits appeals, it negates the restrictive provision. Therefore the correct label is -1, matching the first-round coder.

Provision: PERMISSIVE FORMATION PROVISION 2. [Agency] [must] [explain precise legal definitions of CSOs that it regulates] [at law’s commencement] [or else it is negligent in its duties]
Evidence: Section I, General Provisions – Art. 6(1): “The charitable organization shall be a nongovernment (non-state and non-municipal) nonprofit organization, set up to realize the goals stipulated by the present Federal Law…”.  Art. 7 further specifies the permissible legal forms (public organizations, funds, institutions).
Explanation: The statute itself, at the very beginning of the law, provides a clear legal definition of the type of CSO it governs (“charitable organization”) and enumerates its allowable organizational forms. This satisfies the matrix requirement that precise CSO definitions be supplied at the law’s commencement. Therefore the presence label 1 assigned by the first-round coder is correct.

Provision: RESTRICTIVE FORMATION PROVISION 3. [CSOs] [must] [reregister or otherwise apply for continuation of the organization] [on a certain day, after a fixed duration, or following meaningful changes to the organization] such as renaming the society, amending its constitution, or becoming a branch of another organization [or else face penalty for non-compliance]

Explanation: The law explicitly obliges existing charitable organizations (CSOs) to reregister by a fixed deadline (before July 1, 1999). Failure to comply results in liquidation via court action. Therefore the provision is correctly coded as present (1).

Provision: PERMISSIVE FORMATION PROVISION 3. [Agency] [must not] [reject registration for reasons other than those explicitly stated] [after law’s commencement] [or else it is overstepping its authority]
Evidence: Article 9(2): "The refusal of the state registration of a charitable organization in connection with its legal address being given to it by a citizen at the place of his residence shall be inadmissible."
Explanation: Article 9(2) merely prohibits the registration authority from relying on one specific ground (use of a residential address) when refusing registration. The article does not state that refusals are limited to an exhaustive, expressly enumerated list of grounds, nor does it establish a general rule that the agency may only deny registration for reasons explicitly provided in the law. Because the statute does not impose the broader limitation required by the matrix provision—i.e., that registration may not be rejected for any unstated reason—the provision is not implemented in the legal text. Therefore the correct label is 0 (absence).

Provision: PERMISSIVE FORMATION PROVISION 4. [Agency] [must not] [make registration unnecessarily complex or burdensome] [after law’s commencement] [or else it is overstepping its authority]
Evidence: Article 9(2): "The refusal of the state registration of a charitable organization in connection with its legal address being given to it by a citizen at the place of his residence shall be inadmissible."
Explanation: Article 9(2) forbids the registration authority from refusing registration on one specific ground (use of a residential address). The matrix provision, however, requires a broader rule that the agency "must not make registration unnecessarily complex or burdensome" in general. The legal text does not articulate such a general prohibition; it merely removes a single potential obstacle. Because the aim element of the ADICO structure (avoiding unnecessary complexity or burden in registration) is not fully or explicitly addressed, the provision should be coded as absent (0), not present (1).

Provision: PERMISSIVE FORMATION PROVISION 6. [CSOs] [must] [produce governing document for self-management] such as bylaws minimally prescribed in policy [if they seek to be a formal organization] [or else face penalty for non-compliance]

Evidence: Art. 9(3): "The decision on the refusal of the state registration of a charitable organization, and also its avoidance of such registration, may be appealed against with the court."

Provision: PERMISSIVE OPERATIONS PROVISION 1. [CSOs] [must] [produce summary of operations and activities for public access] [after law’s commencement] [or else face penalty for non-compliance]
Evidence: Article 19(5): "The charitable organization shall provide for an open access, including for the mass media, to its annual reports."
Explanation: The statute expressly obliges charitable organizations (a category of CSO) to make their annual reports openly accessible to the public and the media. Annual reports constitute a summary of the organization’s operations and activities. The imperative language ("shall") satisfies the deontic "must" element; the obligation is ongoing after the law’s commencement; an explicit sanction is not required for the provision to count as present. Hence the provision is correctly coded as present (1).

Provision: PERMISSIVE OPERATIONS PROVISION 2. [CSOs] [must not] [pursue certain operational activities due to their legal type and irrespective of other matters] such as when the activity is incongruent with the legal type—e.g., public charities shall not endorse political candidates; the organization is unlawful; or the CSO’s legal status has been legally revoked [after law’s commencement] [or else face penalty for non-compliance]

Explanation: The statute expressly prohibits charitable organizations (a specific CSO legal type) from supporting political parties or campaigns. This satisfies the ADICO elements: Attribute (charitable organizations), Deontic (shall not have the right), Aim (provide support to political parties), and the temporal condition is implicitly prospective upon the law’s commencement. No ‘or else’ clause is required. Therefore the provision is present, and the first-round coder’s label of 1 is correct.

Provision: RESTRICTIVE OPERATIONS PROVISION 3. [CSOs] [must not] [exceed specific threshold of budget spent on overhead] such as a certain percentage of budgets spent on administrative costs [after law’s commencement] [or else face penalty for non-compliance]
Evidence: Article 16(3): “A charitable organization shall not have the right to use for the remuneration of the labour of the administrative-managerial personnel over 20 per cent of the financial means, which this organization spends in the course of the fiscal year.”
Explanation: The statute expressly forbids charitable organizations (a category of CSOs) from spending more than 20 % of their annual financial means on administrative-managerial personnel remuneration, establishing a concrete overhead cap. The wording “shall not have the right to use … over 20 per cent” conveys a mandatory prohibition (deontic ‘must not’). Thus the legal text implements the matrix provision, making the presence label (1) correct.

Provision: PERMISSIVE OPERATIONS PROVISION 5. [CSO] [may] [use foreign funds for certain activities because its legal definition either expressly permits it or does not explicitly prohibit it] [after law’s commencement] [or else choose not to accept the funds]
Evidence: Article 21(4): "A charitable organization shall have the right to accept charity donations from the foreign citizens, from the stateless persons, and also from the foreign and international organizations."
Explanation: The statute expressly states that charitable organizations (a category of CSO) "shall have the right" (i.e., may) to accept donations from foreign and international sources. This directly permits CSOs to receive—and hence use—foreign funds. All required ADICO elements are satisfied: Attribute (CSO), Deontic (may/shall have the right), Aim (accept/use foreign funds), Condition (after the law’s commencement is implicit), with the or-else clause not necessary. Therefore the provision is present and the first-round coder’s label of 1 is correct.

Provision: RESTRICTIVE OPERATIONS PROVISION 6. Explanation: The statute imposes concrete, legally binding internal-administration rules on charitable organizations: it sets mandatory composition rules for the highest management body (Art. 10(3)) and obliges every organization to maintain bookkeeping records and submit reports (Art. 19(1)). These provisions expressly require CSOs to follow prescribed internal administrative procedures, satisfying the matrix requirement. Therefore the presence label (1) assigned by the first-round coder is correct.

The cited article confers a general freedom to engage in charitable activities but is silent on any notification requirement—or exemption—from local government. Because the law never explicitly says that notification is unnecessary, the provision is not satisfied; the correct label is 0 (absence).
